</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="2"><p><strong>A</strong>. I believe there are many ways we can show kindness through volunteering. I’m retired now, and I currently help build houses for people in need. I work with a volunteering organisation that already has clear plans in place. Through this work, I’ve had the chance to experience different foreign cultures. We’re often sent to various countries to carry out these projects, so it’s also a great way to travel while doing something meaningful. The job involves manual labour, so we’re able to improve our physical health – something that some people only begin to notice after a while.</p>

### **Part 5: Long Text Comprehension - Questions 23–29**

| **Mountain (2026)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |                                         |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| 1\. For centuries, physical features such as height and steepness were the main criteria used to distinguish a mountain from a hill. Yet those measurements do not always settle the question: a modest peak may dominate local history, while a taller one may barely stand out from a plateau. Modern discussions therefore take account of prominence, landscape, local usage, and even the meaning attached to a place by the people who live nearby.                                                                     | **Changing the definition of mountain** |
| 2\. Success in many sports can be measured by a score, a medal, or a finishing time. Reaching a summit is different because the result is inseparable from the climber's private struggle with fear, exhaustion, weather, and self-doubt. Two people may stand on the same peak but experience entirely different journeys. What matters most is often not the altitude itself, but the knowledge that a limit once thought fixed has been surpassed.                                                                         | **Unique sense of achievement**         |
| 3\. A summit photograph once remained in a family album or a climber's personal journal. Today, an ascent may be followed in real time by thousands of viewers, promoted by sponsors, and judged through likes and comments. This exposure can motivate others to attempt difficult goals, but it can also shift attention from the experience itself to the image created around it. The climb becomes something performed for an audience as well as remembered by the individual.                                          | **Publicity of achievement**            |
| 4\. Preparing for a major expedition can demand months of training, substantial savings, and long periods away from home. For some climbers, the next ascent gradually becomes more important than work, family commitments, or financial security. Because determination is widely admired, this imbalance may be praised rather than questioned. The difficulty lies in recognizing when devotion to a demanding goal has stopped enriching life and begun to damage the responsibilities that make ordinary life possible. | **Misguided priorities**                |
| 5\. People who face danger together often develop loyalty more quickly than those who meet in ordinary settings. Yet a group built around risk can develop its own expectations, making caution appear weak and withdrawal feel like betrayal. Members may encourage one another to continue despite poor weather, fatigue, or inadequate preparation. The same bond that provides trust and support can therefore make it harder for an individual to challenge a reckless decision.                                         | **Worrying connections**                |
| 6\. After years of planning expeditions around uncertain weather and seasonal work, some experienced climbers begin to value what they once considered ordinary. A reliable income, regular time with family, and a permanent home may offer a form of satisfaction that constant movement cannot provide. This does not necessarily mean abandoning adventure. Rather, it reflects a shift toward building a life in which occasional risk is supported by dependable routines and long-term commitments.                    | **Focus on stability**                  |
| 7\. A difficult ascent can expose qualities that remain hidden in everyday life. Partners must decide whether to share equipment, slow down for one another, admit fear, and accept help without resentment. When these decisions are handled with honesty, the experience can create a level of trust that ordinary social occasions rarely produce. The mountain is important less as a romantic setting than as a demanding environment in which care, patience, and reliability become impossible to fake.                | **Intimate relationships**              |

| **Digital innovation (2026)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |                                                          |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| 8\. Leisure was once separated fairly clearly from work and study: people left the workplace, met friends, played sport, or settled down with a book. Connected devices have blurred those boundaries. A person may watch a series while replying to colleagues, compete with strangers in an online game, or learn a skill through short videos. Time off has become more personalized and available on demand, but it is also more fragmented and less clearly protected from other obligations.                                                  | **Redefining Leisure in the Digital era**                |
| 9\. Distance no longer requires people to wait for a letter or arrange an expensive international call. A family can maintain an ongoing group conversation across several time zones, while colleagues can exchange voice notes, documents, and live video from different countries. These exchanges are not identical to meeting in person, and constant contact can sometimes feel demanding. Even so, portable software has made relationships easier to maintain when regular face-to-face contact is impossible.                              | **Enhancing connectivity with mobile apps**              |
| 10\. Knowing where to tap on a screen is no longer enough for effective participation in modern society. Online users must judge whether a source is reliable, recognize manipulated content, manage passwords, understand what information they are giving away, and communicate without causing harm. These abilities affect schoolwork, employment, banking, and access to public services. People who lack them may own modern devices yet still be excluded from many of the opportunities those devices appear to provide.                    | **Promoting essential digital literacy**                 |
| 11\. Many online services are designed to remove natural stopping points. One episode begins after another, games offer continuous rewards, and feeds supply new content whenever the screen is refreshed. As a result, users may continue far longer than they intended. The cost is not limited to lost time: late-night use can disturb sleep, prolonged sitting replaces movement, and online contact may crowd out richer social experiences. Enjoyment becomes a problem when the design of the service makes moderation unusually difficult. | **Risks of Excessive Screen-Based Entertainment**        |
| 12\. A weather application may request location access, while a shopping site records searches, purchases, and the time spent viewing each product. Individually, these details can seem harmless; combined over months, they reveal routines, preferences, and likely future behavior. Most users never see the profiles built from this information or the companies with which it is exchanged. The central issue is therefore not simply what people choose to post, but what is gathered quietly while they use ordinary services.             | **Concerns About Data Privacy**                          |
| 13\. Bringing people from different backgrounds into the same online space does not automatically make that space welcoming. New members may leave when jokes rely on stereotypes, aggressive voices dominate discussion, or reporting systems fail to protect those being targeted. Clear rules, active moderation, accessible features, and a willingness to listen are therefore essential. Diversity can be sustained only when participation feels safe and when disagreement does not become a reason to exclude or humiliate others.         | **Building Inclusive and Respectful Online Communities** |
| 14\. A product may contain advanced technology and still be frustrating to use. Small text, unclear symbols, crowded menus, or steps that depend on perfect vision and movement can turn a simple task into an obstacle. Effective development begins by observing a wide range of users rather than expecting everyone to adapt to the system. When complexity is hidden, instructions are clear, and different abilities are considered, sophisticated tools can feel simple without becoming less powerful.                                      | **Prioritize human-friendly designs**                    |

| **The Arrival of the Four-Day Work Week (2026)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |                                             |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| 15\. The familiar Monday-to-Friday timetable emerged from an industrial world in which output was closely connected to time spent beside a machine. Much contemporary work is organized differently: teams collaborate across locations, software completes routine tasks, and results can matter more than visible attendance. Keeping the same pattern simply because it is familiar may therefore be inefficient. The current debate asks whether a schedule designed for an earlier economy still suits organizations whose work, technology, and employees have changed substantially. | **A way of life now out of date**           |
| 16\. An additional non-working day gives staff room to deal with appointments, domestic tasks, and recovery without using annual leave. Some return with greater concentration because they have had enough time to rest rather than spending the weekend catching up on obligations. Families may also coordinate childcare more easily, and staff gain more control over their lives. These improvements can strengthen morale and reduce the temptation to seek another job, even when total pay remains unchanged.                                                                      | **Benefits for employees**                  |
| 17\. A reduced schedule does not automatically reduce the number of customers, patients, or calls that an organization must handle. To maintain coverage, an employer may need overlapping teams, additional recruitment, or overtime payments. Smaller firms with narrow profit margins may find these arrangements difficult to absorb. If wages are cut instead, staff carry the cost; if prices rise, customers do. The model can therefore create expenses that are easy to overlook when attention is focused only on its social appeal.                                              | **Undesirable financial consequences**      |
| 18\. When five days of tasks are compressed into four, the timetable may become more intense rather than more efficient. Meetings are placed closer together, messages accumulate during the extra day off, and delays occur when partner organizations follow a different schedule. Employees who need quiet time for complex work may discover that every available hour has been filled. These effects are not always visible during a short trial, but they can emerge once unusual deadlines, absences, and seasonal demand test the new arrangement.                                  | **Unforeseen challenges for employees**     |
| 19\. Changing the calendar is easier than changing assumptions about what a committed employee looks like. Some managers continue to trust people they can see at a desk, while workers may feel guilty for leaving after completing their tasks. Families and transport arrangements are also built around familiar hours. Even when evidence supports a new pattern, routines developed over many years can make it feel risky or improper. Successful adoption therefore depends on changing expectations as well as updating contracts.                                                 | **Difficult to change old habits**          |
| 20\. A software company may close on Friday with little disruption, but a hospital, hotel, transport service, or shop cannot simply stop serving the public. Employees in these sectors might receive fewer advantages or be asked to work longer shifts while office staff enjoy an extra day away. Differences also arise between salaried and hourly workers. Unless the policy is carefully designed, a reform presented as progress could widen existing divisions between occupations and employment conditions.                                                                      | **Unfair for some people**                  |
| 21\. Organizations do not have to choose between the traditional timetable and one fixed replacement. Some allow staff to select different days away, others shorten each working day, and certain teams alternate their schedules so that services remain available. Seasonal arrangements may also suit businesses whose workload changes during the year. Testing several models can preserve the advantages of greater control and recovery without forcing every workplace to operate according to a pattern that ignores its particular demands.                                      | **Alternative solutions worth considering** |

| **Tech Forward (2026)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |                                                     |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| 22\. Keyboards and touchscreens once defined most contact with digital devices. Increasingly, systems respond to spoken requests, body movement, gaze, and facial expression. These methods can reduce the distance between intention and action: a driver can request directions without looking away from the road, while a person with limited hand movement can control equipment independently. As interfaces become less dependent on technical commands, using a machine begins to resemble communicating with another participant rather than operating a complicated tool. | **Redefining human-technology interaction**         |
| 23\. In many offices, valuable time is consumed by copying information between systems, sorting routine requests, and preparing standard reports. Software can now complete much of this work continuously and with fewer simple errors. The greatest gain does not come merely from doing the same tasks faster. It comes from allowing employees to spend more attention on judgment, design, negotiation, and unusual cases—activities in which experience and creativity matter more than repetition.                                                                           | **Enhancing productivity through smart automation** |
| 24\. Schools once treated computing as a specialist subject for a small group of students. It is now appearing across the curriculum: pupils may program sensors in science, analyze large data sets in geography, or build simple machines in design classes. Such activities teach more than the operation of current devices. They require learners to break problems into steps, test assumptions, and improve a solution after failure, preparing them for occupations that may not yet have familiar names.                                                                   | **Promoting tech-driven education programs**        |
| 25\. Convenient interfaces reduce effort, but they can also remove useful forms of practice. Navigation software may weaken people's awareness of their surroundings, automatic suggestions can replace careful writing, and constant switching between notifications makes sustained attention harder. The concern is not that screens are inherently harmful. It is that handing every small decision to a device may gradually reduce confidence and ability when the device is absent, inaccurate, or unable to understand an unfamiliar situation.                             | **Overreliance on digital interfaces**              |
| 26\. A public service may move online because digital delivery is cheaper and faster for most citizens. Yet the change can disadvantage households with unreliable connections, shared phones, limited data, or little confidence using formal websites. The same barrier affects applications for work, access to lessons, and medical appointments. Providing a device alone is rarely sufficient; affordable connections, accessible services, technical support, and safe places to use them are all necessary if technological progress is not to deepen existing inequality.  | **Concerns about technology access disparities**    |
| 27\. Many successful projects begin outside formal companies or universities. Enthusiasts meet in local workshops, online forums, or volunteer groups to exchange code, lend equipment, and challenge one another's ideas. A beginner may receive guidance from an experienced engineer, while a researcher discovers an unexpected use for an unfinished prototype. These networks are valuable because knowledge moves freely across occupations and age groups, allowing promising ideas to develop before they attract money or institutional support.                          | **Building innovative tech communities**            |
| 28\. The environmental cost of a digital product is often hidden behind its clean screen. Devices require mined materials, data centers consume large amounts of electricity, and frequent upgrades create difficult waste. Some firms are responding by extending software support, designing products that can be repaired, reusing components, and powering infrastructure with lower-carbon energy. The aim is not to stop technological progress, but to judge innovation partly by how long it lasts and what resources it consumes throughout its life.                      | **Focusing on sustainable digital solutions**       |

(2026)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |                                               |

| 36\. A person may follow an excellent exercise plan and still feel unwell because of persistent stress, poor sleep, isolation, or an unsuitable working environment. | **Cultural Exchange (2026)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                                                |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| 155\. People can encounter foreign music, films, food, and opinions without leaving home, but exposure alone does not guarantee understanding. New customs are often interpreted through assumptions learned in one's own society. Real learning begins when individuals ask why a practice matters to those who follow it and accept that familiar behavior is not universally normal. Repeated contact can then replace a simple contrast between 'us' and 'them' with a more complex view of how identity and tradition are formed.                                                     | **Redefining Global Cultural Understanding**   |

The result is often greater confidence in speaking and a less simplified picture of the people whose language they are studying.                       | **Promoting Language Exchange Programs**       |
| 158\. Tourism can provide income that helps maintain historic buildings and traditional crafts. Problems arise when ceremonies are shortened for tour schedules, sacred practices are performed repeatedly for photographs, or local goods are redesigned only to match visitors' expectations. Residents may then earn money from a version of their culture over which they have little control. | 159\. A tradition rarely disappears in a single moment. At the same time, refusing all change can turn heritage into something displayed rather than lived. | **Tulips (2025)**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |                                       |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| 162\. During the Dutch Golden Age in the 17th century, the Netherlands experienced a period of immense wealth and cultural development. Trade, science, and the arts flourished, creating a thriving middle class with disposable income. This prosperity led to a growing interest in luxury items, including rare flowers such as tulips. The booming economy encouraged speculative investments, and tulips quickly became a symbol of wealth and social status. Their rising popularity was not merely about beauty but about prestige-owning exotic tulips was a way to showcase one's success in this golden era. | **The economy during the Golden Age** |
| 163\. Tulips first gained popularity in the Ottoman Empire and later spread to Western Europe. When they arrived in the Netherlands, they became an instant sensation. Their bold colors and unique shapes captivated people, and soon tulips were planted in aristocratic gardens and depicted in still-life paintings. The flower’s visual appeal made it highly desirable among the wealthy and artistic communities. By the early 1600s, tulips had become one of the most fashionable items in Dutch society, and their fame began to outshine other plants traditionally valued in Europe.                        | **Coming into fashion**               |
| 164\. As their popularity increased, tulips transitioned from decorative items to commodities. They began to be sold in markets, sometimes even before they had bloomed. Merchants treated tulip bulbs like valuable assets, often purchasing them based on future availability. Buyers and sellers exchanged contracts instead of the actual flowers, betting on future prices. This speculative behavior turned the tulip into more than just a flower-it became a financial instrument, with its value fluctuating daily based on market trends and demand.                                                          | **An object of trade**                |
| 165\. There are hundreds of tulip varieties, differing in color, shape, and pattern. Some of the most prized tulips during the 17th century were those with unique stripes or flame-like markings on their petals. These effects were later discovered to be caused by a virus affecting the flower, but at the time they were considered extremely rare and beautiful. Breeders carefully cultivated new hybrids, and collectors paid large sums for bulbs with unusual appearances. This diversity in types helped fuel the tulip craze, as people competed to own the most exotic specimens.                         | **Different types of tulip**          |
| 166\. The tulip trade operated on a complex system of contracts, options, and informal agreements. Because bulbs bloom only once a year, buyers often agreed on future purchases, sometimes without even seeing the flower. Specialized markets were established where traders could buy and sell tulip futures. Prices were agreed upon months in advance, and payments were made when the bulbs were delivered. This abstract trading model made it easier for speculators to participate, but it also disconnected the trade from the real value of the product itself.                                              | **Trade mechanics**                   |
| 167\. Tulip trading wasn’t limited to the Netherlands. As demand grew, bulbs were shipped across Europe-from France to England and beyond. Traders carried these rare goods by land and sea, navigating a web of routes and tariffs. Each region had its own preferences, and what was fashionable in Amsterdam might not be as popular in Paris. Nonetheless, tulips remained a desirable item among European elites, and international trade routes helped spread both the flower and its financial influence across the continent.                                                                                   | **Trade across Europe**               |
| 168\. The tulip market collapsed suddenly in 1637. After years of increasing prices and wild speculation, confidence disappeared overnight. Buyers stopped showing up to auctions, and contracts became worthless. Panic spread, and traders who had invested heavily were left with massive debts and unsellable bulbs. This event, often referred to as the first economic bubble in history, highlighted the dangers of speculative markets. The tulip crash left a deep impact on the Dutch economy and became a cautionary tale still taught in economics courses today.                                           | **An Unexpected turn of events**      |

### **Part 4: Abstract topic - 3 questions, 1 minute prep, 2 minutes speaking**

<tr class="header">
<th colspan="3"><strong>CORE STORY 1 – STUDY PROJECT AND PRESENTATION</strong></th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>LEARN ONCE: FIXED CORE STORY</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3">Last semester, I worked with three classmates on an English presentation about technology and study habits. We had two weeks to find information, make the slides and practise. I offered to lead the group because everyone had a different timetable. At first, the amount of work seemed difficult, and we did not agree on every idea. I made a shared plan, gave each person a suitable task and arranged two online meetings. On presentation day, I explained our main points and answered questions. I felt nervous, but everything went well, and our lecturer praised our work and teamwork.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><p><strong>COMMON CONCLUSION</strong></p>
<p>Looking back, I learned that good preparation, clear communication and regular effort can turn a difficult task into a successful experience.</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>RELATED MODULES AND TOPICS</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MODULE A – DIFFICULT QUESTION</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MAIN QUESTION (3 source sets)</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="2"><strong>• Talk about a time you received a difficult question.</strong></td>
<td><strong>• Describe a time when you faced a difficult question.</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>SUBQUESTION 1 (3 source sets)<br />
<strong>• How did you deal with the difficult question?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Use CORE STORY 1 + I paused briefly to organise my thoughts, made sure I understood the question and used information from our research. When I was unsure about one detail, I admitted it honestly and offered to check it afterwards.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>SUBQUESTION 2 (3 source sets)<br />
<strong>• Why is it important to think carefully before answering difficult questions?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Thinking carefully prevents wrong or emotional answers. It helps people understand the real problem, choose useful information and communicate a balanced opinion, which is especially valuable in school discussions, interviews and work meetings. + COMMON CONCLUSION</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MODULE B – ACHIEVEMENT</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MAIN QUESTION</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>• Describe a time when you achieved something.</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>SUBQUESTION 1<br />
<strong>• What helped you achieve it?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Use CORE STORY 1 + Clear goals, a realistic schedule and a fair division of duties were very important. Regular practice showed weak points in our presentation, while useful feedback from my teammates allowed us to improve the final result before the deadline.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>SUBQUESTION 2<br />
<strong>• Why do people set goals for themselves?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Goals give direction and turn a general wish into clear progress. A realistic target can also help people stay motivated during a difficult task because each small step gives people proof that their work is useful. + COMMON CONCLUSION</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MODULE C – BUSY TIME</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MAIN QUESTION</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>• Talk about a busy time you had.</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>SUBQUESTION 1<br />
<strong>• How did you manage your time during that busy period?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Use CORE STORY 1 + I broke the workload into smaller tasks, put the most important tasks first and gave each task a deadline. I also switched off unnecessary notifications and used a shared calendar so that the entire group could remain on schedule.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>SUBQUESTION 2<br />
<strong>• Why are people so busy nowadays?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Modern life requires people to balance work or study with family duties, social duties and constant online communication. Also, goals that are not realistic and poor planning can make an already full timetable feel even more tiring. + COMMON CONCLUSION</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MODULE D – LEARNING A NEW SKILL</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MAIN QUESTION (3 source sets)</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="2"><strong>• Describe a time when you learned a new skill.</strong></td>
<td><strong>• Tell me about something new you learned recently.</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>SUBQUESTION 1 (3 source sets)<br />
<strong>• How has that skill helped you since you learned it?</strong><br />
<strong>• How can you use what you learned in real life?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Use CORE STORY 1 + Preparing the presentation taught me to design clearer slides, speak more confidently and use reliable online research tools. I have since applied these skills in other classes, job applications and everyday conversations that require organised explanations.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>SUBQUESTION 2 (3 source sets)<br />
<strong>• Why should people keep learning new skills?</strong><br />
<strong>• Why is it important to keep learning throughout life?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Regular learning keeps people ready for change as technology and workplaces change. It also develops confidence, curiosity and problem-solving ability. Even a small practical skill can create new opportunities and make daily tasks more efficient. + COMMON CONCLUSION</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MODULE E – PLANNING</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MAIN QUESTION (2 source sets)</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>• Talk about a time you spent a lot of time planning something.</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>SUBQUESTION 1 (2 source sets)<br />
<strong>• How did planning help you in that situation?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Use CORE STORY 1 + Our plan showed the whole workload and revealed possible problems early. Because we had clear milestones, we could monitor progress and adjust the schedule when one member became unavailable without missing the final deadline.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>SUBQUESTION 2 (2 source sets)<br />
<strong>• Why is planning important before doing something important?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Planning turns a large goal into easy to manage actions. It helps people use time and resources well, prepare for possible problems and avoid rushed decisions that may reduce the quality of an important piece of work. + COMMON CONCLUSION</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MODULE F – TEAMWORK</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MAIN QUESTION (2 source sets)</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="2"><strong>• Describe a time when you worked in a team.</strong></td>
<td><strong>• Tell me about a time when you worked in a team.</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>SUBQUESTION 1 (2 source sets)<br />
<strong>• What made your team work well together?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Use CORE STORY 1 + We communicated openly, divided the work according to individual strengths and checked one another’s progress. We listened to different opinions, supported anyone who fell behind and made major decisions together rather than letting one person dominate.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>SUBQUESTION 2 (2 source sets)<br />
<strong>• Why is teamwork important at school or at work?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Difficult tasks often require different skills and views. Effective teamwork reduces individual pressure, improves problem-solving and teaches people to solve disagreements, communicate and take responsibility for a shared result. + COMMON CONCLUSION</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MODULE G – GREAT EFFORT</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MAIN QUESTION (3 source sets)</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="2"><strong>• Describe a time when you made a great effort.</strong></td>
<td><strong>• Talk about a time you had to put in a lot of effort.</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>SUBQUESTION 1 (3 source sets)<br />
<strong>• What motivated you to keep trying?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Use CORE STORY 1 + I focused on the progress we had already made rather than the work that remained. My teammates encouraged me whenever I felt tired, and the desire to produce something we could really be proud of kept me moving forward.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>SUBQUESTION 2 (3 source sets)<br />
<strong>• Why is effort important for achieving success?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Special achievements rarely happen immediately. Consistent effort helps people to correct mistakes, build confidence and continue despite setbacks. Even when the outcome is imperfect, sustained practice normally leads to valuable improvement. + COMMON CONCLUSION</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MODULE H – ASKING A GOOD QUESTION</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MAIN QUESTION</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>• A Time you Asked a Good Question.</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>SUBQUESTION 1<br />
<strong>• Why was that question useful or important?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Use CORE STORY 1 + I asked whether the information in a popular online article came from a reliable original study. That question encouraged the group to check the source, replace a weak statistic and make our presentation much more credible.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>SUBQUESTION 2<br />
<strong>• Why is asking good questions important for learning?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">A careful question shows what people do not understand and encourages deeper thinking instead of only memorising facts. It can also guide discussion, challenge ideas people accept without checking and help both the speaker and the listener discover a clearer explanation.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MODULE I – ENGLISH COURSE</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MAIN QUESTION (2 source sets)</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>• Talk about a time you attended an English course.</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>SUBQUESTION 1 (2 source sets)<br />
<strong>• How did the course improve your English?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Use CORE STORY 1 + The course gave me regular speaking practice and detailed feedback on pronunciation, grammar and organisation. Group presentations also taught me to express ideas more naturally, respond to unexpected questions and speak despite feeling nervous.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>SUBQUESTION 2 (2 source sets)<br />
<strong>• Why do so many people want to learn English today?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">English gives access to international schools, digital resources and a wider range of careers. It also helps people to communicate while travelling and to build relationships with colleagues or friends from different countries. + COMMON CONCLUSION</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MODULE J – OVERCOMING A CHALLENGE</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MAIN QUESTION</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>• Talk about a challenge you have faced.</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>SUBQUESTION 1<br />
<strong>• How did you overcome the challenge?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Use CORE STORY 1 + The main challenge was organising people with different schedules while dealing with a large amount of information. I solved it by setting priorities, asking for help when necessary and reviewing our progress every two days.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>SUBQUESTION 2<br />
<strong>• Why can challenges be useful for personal growth?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Challenges force people to leave familiar routines and develop new strategies. Although they can be uncomfortable, they often strengthen mental strength, reveal hidden abilities and give lessons that make future problems easier to manage. + COMMON CONCLUSION</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MODULE K – TECHNOLOGY HELPED ME</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MAIN QUESTION</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>• Tell me about a time when technology helped you.</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>SUBQUESTION 1<br />
<strong>• How did technology make things easier for you?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Use CORE STORY 1 + A shared document and video-meeting platform allowed us to work from different places, edit the same material and receive updates immediately. Without those tools, arranging meetings and combining everyone’s research would have taken far longer.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>SUBQUESTION 2<br />
<strong>• Why do people use so much technology nowadays?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">People depend on technology because it saves time, improves access to information and allows instant communication. When used responsibly, it can do repeated tasks and help people study, work and solve problems more effectively. + COMMON CONCLUSION</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MODULE L – MAJOR RESPONSIBILITY</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MAIN QUESTION</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>• Tell me about a time when you had a major responsibility.</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>SUBQUESTION 1<br />
<strong>• How did you manage that responsibility?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Use CORE STORY 1 + As group coordinator, I set deadlines, monitored progress and made sure quieter members could help. I kept a checklist, followed up politely and prepared a backup plan in case a teammate was absent on presentation day.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>SUBQUESTION 2<br />
<strong>• Why is learning to be responsible important?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Responsibility teaches people to consider how their actions affect others. It builds reliability, self-discipline and trust, qualities that are very important for independent living as well as successful study and jobs. + COMMON CONCLUSION</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MODULE M – GIVING A PRESENTATION</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MAIN QUESTION</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>• Talk about a presentation you gave to other people.</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>SUBQUESTION 1<br />
<strong>• What helped you give the presentation successfully?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Use CORE STORY 1 + Thorough research, simple slides and repeated rehearsal made the presentation successful. I practised transitions with my teammates, prepared for possible questions and concentrated on speaking slowly rather than memorising every sentence.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>SUBQUESTION 2<br />
<strong>• Why are presentation skills important at school and at work?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Presentation skills help people explain difficult information clearly, persuade an audience and respond confidently to questions. They are useful in classrooms, interviews, meetings and almost any job that involves sharing ideas. + COMMON CONCLUSION</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MODULE N – TRYING SOMETHING NEW</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MAIN QUESTION</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>• Talk about a time when you tried something new.</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>SUBQUESTION 1<br />
<strong>• How did you feel after trying it?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Use CORE STORY 1 + Volunteering to lead the presentation was new and at first frightening. Afterwards, I felt relieved and really proud because the experience proved that I could remain calm, organise others and communicate effectively under pressure.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>SUBQUESTION 2<br />
<strong>• Why should people sometimes try new things?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">New experiences broaden people’s view and reveal abilities they may not know they possess. They also reduce fear of new situations and make life more varied, provided the risks are considered sensibly. + COMMON CONCLUSION</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MODULE O – CHANGING SCHOOLS</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MAIN QUESTION</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>• Tell me about a time when you changed schools. Say why the change happened, how you felt at first, what helped you settle in, and explain what schools can do to welcome new students.</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>SUBQUESTION 1<br />
<strong>• What helped you settle into the new school?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Use CORE STORY 1 + When I changed schools, joining a study group helped me settle in quickly. Friendly classmates explained the timetable, shared notes and invited me to work on the presentation, so I gradually felt included rather than isolated.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>SUBQUESTION 2<br />
<strong>• Why is it important for schools to help new students feel welcome?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">A helpful welcome reduces anxiety and allows new students to focus on learning. Schools can assign a buddy, explain routines clearly and create group activities so that friendships form naturally. + COMMON CONCLUSION</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">

<td colspan="3"><strong>• Tell me about some interesting information that you learned recently. Say what it was, where you found it, why it interested you, and explain whether people should check information before sharing it.</strong></td>

<tr class="odd">
<td>SUBQUESTION 1<br />
<strong>• How did that information change your understanding of the topic?</strong></td>

<tr class="even">
<td>SUBQUESTION 2<br />
<strong>• Why should people check information before sharing it?</strong></td>

</tr>

<td colspan="3"><strong>CORE STORY 2 – A MEMORABLE TRIP AND DISCOVERY</strong></td>

<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3">Last summer, I travelled to Da Nang with two close friends for three days. We went by overnight train and stayed in a small hotel near the river. We visited a museum, walked around an old building, climbed a green hill and tried several local dishes. One afternoon, heavy rain changed our plan, and my phone lost its signal for a while. We stayed calm and asked a shopkeeper for directions. The journey was tiring, and a few things went wrong, but we helped one another, met friendly local people and learned a lot about the area.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><p><strong>COMMON CONCLUSION</strong></p>
<p>The trip taught me that curiosity, flexibility and simple preparation can make a new experience safer and more enjoyable.</p></td>

<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>MAIN QUESTION</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>• Tell me about a time when someone gave you a compliment.</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>SUBQUESTION 1<br />
<strong>• How did the compliment make you feel?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Use CORE STORY 3 + The organiser complimented me on explaining the activity patiently to the children. I felt appreciated and more confident because the comment recognised a specific action rather than offering empty praise.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>SUBQUESTION 2<br />
<strong>• Why can giving sincere compliments be important?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">A sincere compliment reinforces positive behaviour and can improve someone’s confidence at very little cost. It is most effective when it is specific, honest and delivered without comparing the person negatively with others. + COMMON CONCLUSION</td>
</tr>

</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td>SUBQUESTION 1<br />
<strong>• How did the activity help you or other people?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Use CORE STORY 3 + The event gave children a safe creative activity, helped older residents become more comfortable with technology and connected neighbours who had rarely spoken. It also taught volunteers to organise resources and respond to different needs.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>SUBQUESTION 2<br />
<strong>• Why should people take part in volunteer or community activities?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Volunteering addresses local needs while developing empathy, teamwork and practical skills. It also gives people a stronger connection to their community and shows that small contributions can produce a special shared impact. + COMMON CONCLUSION</td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3"><strong>CORE STORY 4 – SAVING FOR AN IMPORTANT PURCHASE</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><strong>LEARN ONCE: FIXED CORE STORY</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td colspan="3">Earlier this year, my old laptop stopped working well while I was doing university assignments, so I decided to replace it. The model I liked was too expensive, and I could not buy it at once. Instead of borrowing money, I compared different laptops, set a savings goal and wrote down my daily spending. I cooked at home more often, avoided things I did not need and took some small weekend jobs. After three months, I saved enough for a reliable mid-priced laptop. The process needed patience, but it helped me value the laptop and use it more carefully.</td>
</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td colspan="3"><p><strong>COMMON CONCLUSION</strong></p>
<p>The experience taught me to separate real needs from short-term wants and to make careful decisions about money.</p></td>
</tr>

<td colspan="3"><strong>RELATED MODULES AND TOPICS</strong></td>

</tr>
<tr class="odd">
<td>SUBQUESTION 2 (2 source sets)<br />
<strong>• Why do people sometimes want things they cannot have?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Scarcity can make an item appear more valuable, while advertising and social comparison create goals that are not realistic. People may also connect possessions with status or happiness, even when a cheaper option would meet their actual needs. + COMMON CONCLUSION</td>
</tr>

<strong>• What helped you save enough money?</strong></td>

<tr class="even">
<td>SUBQUESTION 2 (3 source sets)<br />
<strong>• Why is saving money important for young people?</strong></td>
<td colspan="2">Savings give protection against emergencies and make schools, travel or major purchases possible without excessive debt. Starting early also develops self-control and allows compound interest to work over a longer period. + COMMON CONCLUSION</td>

After a month, I felt more organised and confident.</td>

## Writing

### **Part 1: Word-level writing - 5 short answers**

| What is your job?                          | A digital marketing specialist. |

<p>First, the club should reduce energy use and renegotiate supplier contracts first. This would cut costs with limited impact. I also recommend that it keep the café but shorten its quiet-hour opening schedule, which would retain an important social space. In addition, it would be useful to survey members and publish the savings target.</p>
<p>Together, these measures could make transparent savings without seriously weakening the club while addressing members’ concerns in a fair and practical way. Thank you for considering my suggestions. I hope they will help the club make an inclusive and well-informed decision.</p>
<p>Yours faithfully,</p>
<p>Sam Nguyen</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<th colspan="2"><p>Dear members,</p>
<p>Our Fashion Club is planning a special fashion event next month, and we would like to hear your views.</p>
<p>We are considering two options. The first is an online fashion event, where members can watch presentations, meet designers online and ask questions from home.</p>
<p>The second option is a live event with a fashion show, where members can meet in person, see new clothes and designs, and take part in other fashion activities.</p>
<p>Please tell us which option you prefer and explain why. We would also like to hear any suggestions you have for making the event interesting and enjoyable.</p>
<p>Fashion Club Manager</p></th>
</tr>

<tr class="odd">

<p>Best,</p>
<p>Sam</p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="even">
<td><strong>Write to the Fashion Club manager. Explain whether you would prefer the online fashion event or the live event with a fashion show. Give reasons for your choice and suggest how the event could be organised successfully.</strong></td>
<td><p>Dear Club Manager,</p>
<p>I am writing in response to the recent notice about the two fashion-event options. I find the situation exciting. Overall, I believe the live fashion show would offer a richer experience.</p>
<p>First, the club should combine designer presentations with a well-paced runway show. This would let members examine designs and meet creators. I also recommend that it stream the main sessions and accept online questions, which would include members who cannot travel. In addition, it would be useful to add a styling workshop and sustainable-fashion display.</p>
<p>Together, these measures could create an inclusive event with strong educational value while addressing members’ concerns in a fair and practical way. Thank you for considering my suggestions. I hope they will help the club make an inclusive and well-informed decision.</p>
<p>Yours faithfully,</p>
<p>Sam Nguyen</p></td>

> Công thức speaking:
>
> **<u>1. Giới thiệu</u>**
>
> **Giới thiệu số lượng**
>
> There is + a/an + n + ...  
> There are + number + plural noun + ...
>
> **Giới thiệu sở hữu**
>
> I have...  
> My ... has...
>
> **<u>2. Miêu tả</u>**
>
> **Miêu tả tính chất**
>
> S + be + adj
>
> **Miêu tả bằng nhiều tính từ**
>
> S + be + adj, adj, and adj
>
> **<u>3. Thói quen</u>**
>
> S + adv of frequency + v
>
> **<u>4. Mục đích</u>**
>
> S + V + to + V
>
> **<u>5. Nguyên nhân</u>**
>
> because + clause
>
> The main reason is that + clause
>
> One thing I really appreciate is that + clause
>
> What I like most is...
>
> Clause, but clause
>
> Although + clause, main clause
>
> Even though + clause, main clause
>
> **<u>7. Thời gian</u>**
>
> Whenever + clause
>
> Since I was + age/time
>
> Growing up,...
>
> **<u>8. Quan hệ</u>**
>
> N+ who + v
>
> N + which + v
>
> Nn + that + v
